title: Henry's inequality conjecture for the Riemann zeta and digamma functions
statement:
Let $\b0$ denote the Euler–Mascheroni constant, and define

$$
b':= \b0+\frac12,\qquad b:= \b0-\frac12.
$$

For $0<s<1$, the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$ and the digamma function $\psi(s)=\frac{\Gamma'(s)}{\Gamma(s)}$ satisfy **Henry's conjecture.**

$$
\pi\cot(\pi s)+s < \zeta(s)-\psi(s) < \pi\cot(\pi s)+b's+b.
$$

The conjecture gives two-sided bounds for the difference between the Riemann zeta and digamma functions on the interval $(0,1)$. The supplied text presents it as a conjecture of Henry but provides no resolution, so its status is open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09276

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).
source_name: Liwen Gao and Xuejun Guo, “Inequalities for ζ(s)-ψ(1-s) related to a conjecture of Henry”, arXiv:2601.09276 (2026).
